newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/3Com busy both ways ahead of Q4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/3Com busy both ways ahead of Q4.

text.p: Options on shares of 3Com Corp were actively traded Tuesday ahead of the company's fiscal fourth quarter earnings, with buyers and sellers busy.
"We've got paper on both sides," a market maker in the options said. "It looks like one of those speculation on good earnings, or better than the Street" expectations.
The First Call consensus for 3Com's fourth quarter is $0.48 per share versus $0.72 per share in the 1996 fiscal fourth quarter. Estimates range as high as $0.51 a share.
In afternoon activity, 3Com shares were up 1-5/8 at 49-7/8 on more than seven million shares turnover.
The heaviest trading in 3Com options was in the July 50 calls, which traded 4,145 contracts.
The July 45 put traded 2,650 and the July 55 call traded nearly 2,600, rounding out the most active.
The market maker said volatilities in 3Com options remained at elevated levels ahead of the earnings.
"It's up significantly in the last three or four days," he said, adding that for the front-month options, volatility was in the low 70's and for back months in the 50's.
"That's about 10 to 20 percent higher than usual," he said.

In other activity, Bristol-Myers Squibb Co options drew interest as the stock rallied sharply after a U.S. Food and Drug Administration advisory panel voted unanimously late Monday to approve the company's Taxol as a second-line therapy for Kaposi's sarcoma, a cancer affecting 20,000 AIDS patients.
Merrill Lynch upgraded its rating on Bristol to long term buy from long term accumulate.
The stock was up 8-5/8 at 85 on more than 5.3 million shares in afternoon activity.
"The stock flew up," said an options market maker. "We had a fast market" in the options.
She said one Wall Street brokerage was a big buyer of Bristol calls early on.
The July 80 and 85 calls were the most active Bristol options in afternoon activity, with turnover of 1,625 and 1,450 contracts, respectively.
The Bristol July 80 put traded 685 contracts, making it the most active put.
The market maker said volatility in the July Bristol options has been fluctuating between around 25 and 27, with volatility in the back month options higher.
In other activity, Philip Morris Cos Inc options remained active at the American Stock Exchange, led by a big roll to the December 50 calls from the September 50 calls.
The September 50 calls, which had open interest of 31,752 through Monday, traded 12,760 contracts and the December 50 call, which had open interest of 4,745 contracts, traded nearly 12,000.
"There's no question, it's all being done as spreads -- rolling," Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said of the action in those two options.
Philip Morris shares were up 1-1/8 at 43-7/8 in afternoon trade.
